entities.name: Adrian Gouffier de Boissy
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adrian Gouffier de Boissy (c. 1479–1523) was a French cardinal and one of the most prominent ecclesiastical figures of the French Renaissance court. A member of the powerful Gouffier family — one of the great court dynasties under Louis XII and Francis I — he was made Cardinal of Boissy in 1515 by Pope Leo X as part of the Franco-papal diplomacy that characterised the early reign of Francis I. His brother Guillaume Gouffier, lord of Bonnivet, was one of Francis I's most intimate companions, giving the family extraordinary court influence.

Adrian Gouffier's cardinalate represents the nepotistic and politically driven character of Renaissance ecclesiastical appointments, in which great family connections were often more important than theological distinction or pastoral achievement. His elevation at approximately 36 years old on the basis of family influence rather than ecclesiastical merit was typical of the Renaissance cardinalate that the Council of Trent would later seek to reform.

His brief career as a cardinal — he died in 1523 at approximately 44 — was conducted at the height of Renaissance court Catholicism in France, when the French Church was deeply integrated into the social and cultural life of the Valois monarchy. His death preceded the outbreak of the French Wars of Religion by four decades, placing him in the last generation of French Catholic leaders who experienced the Reformation only in its earliest stirrings.
